properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 10:25PM MDT until October 23 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of western, central, and north-central New Mexico,
mainly along and west of the Continental Divide.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread showers and thunderstorms will continue moving north
over the region through the predawn hours before tapering off
around sunrise. Additional rain amounts for the rest of tonight
will range from 0.25 inch to 0.75 inch, with locally heavier
amounts up to 1.50 inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 11:36AM PDT until October 23 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Northeastern Lassen County and Surprise valley in
California, and northern Washoe County and northwestern Pershing
County in Nevada. The watch area includes the Biscar and S1-Vya
burn scars.

* WHEN...Through 5 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Small creeks and streams may flood rural roads. Increased
sediment transport from burn scars may clog culverts and ditches.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Storm total rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches, locally 2 inches or
more, is possible through through early Friday. Heavier rain this
afternoon and evening may briefly exceed 0.5 inch per hour.
Runoff may linger overnight.
- Vulnerable locations include remote ranches within and near the
Biscar and S1-Vya burn scars, downstream drainages, and culverts
along US-395 from Stoney Creek Road north to Rye Patch Road.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 11:28AM MDT until October 24 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Animas River At Farmington affecting Northwest Plateau zone.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...Animas River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From Friday evening to Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Portions of the riverwalk in Farmington are
flooded. Local overbank flooding is occurring along the lower
Animas River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 6.4 feet.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached late tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

Residents and those with interests near the river should monitor
rising water levels and be prepared for possible Flood Warnings.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 21 at 5:53AM MST until October 22 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An upper-level trough will bring a deep surge of subtropical and
tropical moisture into our region. Showers and thunderstorms will
develop across much of northern and central Arizona early
Wednesday morning and continue through Thursday evening. Stronger
thunderstorms will bring threats of Flash Flooding, while more
prolonged rainfall could lead to elevated flow in streams,
rivers, and washes.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.
